item.title: Ground stop results in side judge Don Willard serving as referee for two games on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Flight disruptions result in multiple changes to Week 10 officiating assignments.
item.content:encoded:
Friday's nationwide ground stop won't keep NFL teams from getting to their road games on Sunday. It will, however, impact the ability of officials to get to where they need to be.

The NFL has announced that officiating assignments have changed for Week 10. And the situation will result in a backup referee serving as the referee in two games on the same day.

"Due to the ongoing nationwide impact to air travel this weekend, the NFL has adjusted its officiating assignments for Week 10 games, reassigning officials to games within driving distance of their hometowns," the NFL said in a statement. "The changes will necessitate that three backup referees — umpires Barry Anderson and Duane Heydt and side judge Don Willard [pictured] — will work as referees in the following games: Carolina-New Orleans – Duane Heydt; Jacksonville-Tennessee – Barry Anderson; Miami-Indianapolis and Pittsburgh-Cincinnati – Don Willard.

"Each of the league’s 17 officiating crews have a backup referee identified, and that individual trains throughout the year to work at the referee position should the need arise."

The situation creates the likely unprecedented situation of a referee working two games in one day. Willard will handle Dolphins-Colts at 1:00 p.m. ET, and then he'll make the 109-mile trip from Indianapolis to Cincinnati for the Sunday night game.

Making the unprecedented even more unusual is the fact that Willard's usual crew (led by referee Scott Novak) wasn't scheduled to work at all this weekend.

The announcement doesn't address where the referees for those three games will be working, or what their roles will be. Shawn Smith was scheduled to be the referee for Panthers-Saints, Alex Moore was set to be the referee for Jaguars-Titans, Carl Cheffers was due to be the referee for Dolphins-Colts, and Clete Blakeman was slated to be the referee for Steelers-Bengals.

The league's statement also doesn't specify other shifts that were required as to the established crews that work together throughout the regular season.

item.title: Jerry Jones: "I don't think we're far away" from 18 regular-season games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As to the timeline, Jones says, "Next month? No. Next year? Maybe. [The] next year? Maybe."
item.content:encoded:
As the NFL embarks on the second half of its current 18-week regular-season schedule, it's just a matter of time before the current structure changes.

It's no secret that the NFL wants to expand the regular season from 17 to 18 games. The league is sufficiently confident about it happening that folks like Cowboys owner Jerry Jones speak of it as a given.

"I don’t think we’re far away from it," Jones said Friday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, regarding the addition of an extra game. "I don't know how — what is far away. Next month? No. Next year? Maybe. [The] next year? Maybe. That has to be negotiated with the players.

"But it's in everybody's best interests.  You'd cut back on the preseason games. You'd have teams more develop in the first few games as the type of thing you were trying to get done in preseason. But it's in everybody's interest, and it certainly is in the players' best interest in my mind, for sure.  And having said that, I would anticipate that coming."

His comments presume the NFL Players Association will happily agree to 18 regular-season games. They likely won't. At a minimum, they'll seek major concessions in exchange for the willingness to add yet another game that counts.

The unspoken goal had been 2027. The NFL delayed picking a date for Super Bowl LXII in Atlanta in order to accommodate the possibility that the game will slide a week or two deeper into February. That would make 2028 the earliest year for expansion, as a practical matter. (Adding a game for 2027 would be possible only if the dead week between the conference championships is wiped out or if the season starts a week earlier. If an 18th game will result in a second bye, both would be required.)

Expansion by 2027 would require expedited negotiations. Expansion by 2028 would hinge on the NFL and NFLPA striking a deal within the next year or so. The union has shown no inclination, however, to engage in talks aimed at extending the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, which runs through the 2030 season.

Still, if push comes to shove, there will be 18 games. The blueprint was created in 2011. The NFL will lock the players out until the players agree to the things the owners want. Most notably, 18 regular-season games and 16 annual international games.

Beyond that, Jones's comment about the early games of the season is odd. "You'd have teams more develop in the first few games as the type of thing you were trying to get done in preseason."

He says that as if it's a good thing. It definitely is not. Already, teams struggle in September to get up to speed, given that most teams (with the exception of those assigned to the Hall of Fame Game) play only three preseason games. When the preseason reduces to two games, that's even fewer chances to prepare.

It's also fewer chances for the non-starters to get the attention of coaches and General Managers in games that don't count in the standings. It will become harder for undrafted free agents to make the 53-man rosters.

Regardless, the motivation isn't football. It's money. More inventory equals more weekends equals more broadcast windows equals more revenue.

And that likely will continue until the preseason shrinks to zero games — and the regular season expands to 20 games.

item.title: Jared Goff takes 1-3 career record vs. Patriots into Germany game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter.
item.content:encoded:
For his career, Lions quarterback Jared Goff has a record of 101-67-1 as a starter. That's a 59.7-percent win rate.

Against the Patriots, Goff is 1-3. That's a 25-percent win rate.

In those four games, Goff has two touchdown passes and five interceptions.

Sunday's game in Germany will be the first one against the Patriots with a coach other than Bill Belichick. Goff has never faced current Patriots coach Mike Vrabel; during Goff's time as a starter with the Rams and Lions and Vrabel's tenure with the Titans, their two teams never crossed paths.

Goff's first loss to New England came in 2016, in his third career start. The Patriots won, 26-10. Two years later, New England beat Goff and the Rams in the Super Bowl, 13-3.

In 2020, the Patriots beat Goff and the Rams, 24-3. In 2022, the Patriots beat Goff and the Lions, 29-0.

Sunday's game is consequential for both teams. The 6-2 Lions are caught in a cluster of four NFC North teams that all have six or more wins. The Patriots, at 5-4, are fading in the AFC East race and could be scrambling to secure a wild-card spot.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans is getting better, we're trying to make sure he fully heals
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The 49ers have ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans for Sunday's game in Dallas, but head coach Kyle Shanahan says Evans is getting healthy enough to play.
item.content:encoded:
The 49ers have ruled out wide receiver Mike Evans for Sunday's game in Dallas, but head coach Kyle Shanahan says Evans is getting healthy enough to play.

Evans is dealing with Achilles tendinitis and Shanahan said that while Evans' recovery is progressing and he could probably play if he had to, the 49ers want to prioritize his long-term health and not the short-term benefit of having him on the field on Sunday.

"It's been going well. I'm sure if this was the last game or something he'd be able to go out there, but we're just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn't act up again. But it's going in the right direction," Shanahan said.

Although Evans won't play this week, Shanahan said Evans could be good to go for next week's game, Sunday night against the Vikings in Mexico City.

"There's a chance for next week, but not sure yet," Shanahan said.

The 33-year-old Evans was off to an outstanding start this season, and he's the 49ers' team leader with an average of 70 receiving yards per game. The 49ers want to get that production back, but the top priority is having Evans produce in the playoffs.

item.title: Ground stop nudges Ole Miss-Oklahoma game to Sunday (and OU doesn't like that)
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Friday's nationwide shutdown of the aviation system has resulted in a delayed kickoff for several college football games on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
Friday's nationwide shutdown of the aviation system has resulted in a delayed kickoff for several college football games on Saturday. One of them was moved to Sunday — and the home team isn't happy.

The Ole Miss visit to Oklahoma shifted from 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday to Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET.

"The Ole Miss football team was unable to depart Oxford Friday night due to the FAA ground stoppage," the SEC said in a statement. "After the stoppage was lifted, a late-night departure could not be accommodated by the charter company with which Ole Miss was contracted and the team's departure has been delayed until Saturday afternoon."

Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny strenuously objected to the decision to move the game to Sunday.

"After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner [Greg] Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection," Denny said. "He further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit. I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation."

Oklahoma nevertheless will comply with the decision. Even if the Sooners don't like the decision to play the game later.

"Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans," Denny said. "Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference's decision tonight. . . . We are obligated to play the game when directed. But we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening."

On one hand, there's no point huffing and puffing if Oklahoma ultimately wasn't going to blow the house down. On the other hand, the school may have felt compelled to do something to deflect the frustrations of those who weren't happy with having the game moved to the next day.

The bottom line is that the ground stop created travel disruptions and inconveniences for millions of people. And few are thrilled about that.

Oklahoma chose to complain. If it makes them feel better, fine. In the end, it doesn't change the fact that the game will be added to the cluster of NFL games that begin at the same time on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Deion Sanders, Colorado score huge upset over No. 14 Houston
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: After the loss that dropped the Colorado Buffaloes to 3-6, coach Deion Sanders said, among other things, "The fans deserve better."
item.content:encoded:
After the loss that dropped the Colorado Buffaloes to 3-6, coach Deion Sanders said, among other things, "The fans deserve better."

On Friday night, they got it.

Colorado upset No. 14 Houston on Friday night in Boulder. The 42-32 victory moved the Buffaloes to 4-6.

Houston led 20-7 in the first half. Colorado had taken the lead by halftime, 21-20. Eventually, Colorado scored 28 straight points, taking a 35-20 lead.

For Houston, the loss killed any realistic hope of qualifying for the final 12-team College Football Playoff. For Colorado, the win keeps them alive for bowl eligibility — and possibly saves Sanders from having his fourth year in Colorado be his last.

Especially since he has a $25.5 million buyout.

item.title: Saints sent Jordyn Tyson to renowned hamstring specialist at University of Wisconsin
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr.
item.content:encoded:
In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr. Bryan Heiderscheit and his team at the University of Wisconsin to research new ways to prevent and treat hamstring injuries. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson may benefit from that research.

Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports that the Saints sent Tyson on two separate visits to the University of Wisconsin to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team.

Hamstring injuries have been a major problem for Tyson, who was out for three months with a hamstring injury before finally making his NFL debut last week. Tyson also missed time at Arizona State last year because of a hamstring injury, and he didn't run at either Arizona State's Pro Day or the NFL Scouting Combine because of his hamstring.

But there's hope for Tyson after his evaluations in Wisconsin. Heiderscheit was able to identify a weakness with Tyson's hamstring that he thinks can be strengthened with a specific workout regimen that Tyson has been following.

Heiderscheit previously worked with Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and helped him recover from hamstring injuries, and it worked: Watson has started every game this season and in nine games already has career-highs with 49 catches for 879 yards, and he's leading the NFL with an average of 17.9 yards per catch.

That's the kind of player the Saints think Tyson can be, if he can stay healthy. Heiderscheit's treatment may be the key to Tyson staying healthy.

item.title: Joe Burrow can join Peyton Manning as only QBs with 4 total TDs in 5 straight games
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: A big game from Burrow on Sunday night would put him in some very exclusive company in NFL history.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has been racking up touchdowns recently, and if he continues to do it on Sunday night against the Steelers, he'll join some very exclusive company in NFL history.

Burrow has had at least four touchdowns, combined rushing and passing, in each of the last four games. If Burrow has another four-touchdown game on Sunday night, he will join Peyton Manning as the only quarterbacks in NFL history with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in five consecutive games.

Burrow's last four games:
Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons.
Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans.
Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens.
Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins.

Manning became the first quarterback to have five straight games with four touchdowns in Weeks 8-12 of 2004 with the Colts, when he had a six-touchdown game, two five-touchdown games and two four-touchdown games. (All of Manning's touchdowns were passing, not rushing.) Manning was named NFL MVP that season.

And Burrow is an MVP candidate with the way he's playing now. A win over the Steelers on Sunday night would put the Bengals in first place in the AFC North, and a big game with those big stakes would give a big boost to Burrow's MVP chances.

item.title: At least 50 different quarterbacks will have started games through Week 10
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza will make his first career start on Sunday. Two others will make their debuts, too: Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck and Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord.

Via NBC Sports research, they'll become the 48th, 49th, and 50th different quarterbacks to start games during the 2026 season.

It will be only the second time in the last 15 years (excluding the 1987 strike season) during which 50 different quarterbacks have started games in the first 10 weeks of a season.

If, for some reason, another quarterback makes his first start of the season on Sunday (that's unlikely with Seahawks quarterback Drew Lock not having an injury designation for Sunday), it will be the second-most starters through 10 weeks since 1950.

In 1999, 55 different quarterbacks started games through the first 10 weeks of the season.

Most of the changes have arisen from injury. For the Raiders, the transition to Mendoza happened after Kirk Cousins was traded to the Vikings.

item.title: FAA lifts ground stop, clearing the way for NFL teams to travel on Saturday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Eleven teams will be flying for Sunday games.
item.content:encoded:
The ground stop has stopped.

Friday's sudden, and objectively concerning, decision by the FAA to issue only the second nationwide order to keep all planes from flying since 9/11 has ended.

The situation should result in no impact on NFL teams traveling to their road games for Sunday. It also should allow college teams to get to wherever they need to go for Saturday.

If it had happened one day later, the end result could have created chaos for NFL teams, significantly delaying their travel and turning their schedules for the night before the game upside down.

The situation came as a surprise to some NFL teams. For example, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan learned about it during his Friday press conference.

Asked about the ground stop impacting the team's plans for travel to Dallas on Saturday based on the ground stop, Shanahan said, "When did they do that?"

He also asked, "Why'd they do that?"

Eventually, Shanahan said, "I didn't know. I just first heard."

The 49ers plan to leave San Francisco at 1:00 p.m. PT on Saturday. Ten other teams will be traveling on Saturday, too.

item.title: Victims claim Rex Ryan "almost killed" them with truck in Nasvhille
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The victims in last week's Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward.
item.content:encoded:
The victims in last week's Nashville incident involving former NFL coach Rex Ryan have come forward. And they are making specific and clear accusations about Ryan's driving.

Via the California Post, attorney Michael Holland said that Ryan "almost killed" Holland and his wife with Ryan's pickup truck, as they crossed the street.

“If we had been six inches further out,” Holland said, “I’d be in a hospital right now and so would my wife.”

Added Holland regarding Ryan: “He decided he wanted to turn and didn’t care, and just ran over both of my feet, my wife’s foot and got her leg too.”

Holland contends that Ryan didn't stop, and that Holland caught up with the truck and pounded on the window.

“He was told in no uncertain terms what he had done, and instead of staying at the scene or even saying, ‘Sorry,’ he just got back in his vehicle and took off," Holland said.

Holland gave the Post a photo of his wife's injuries.

“I mean, just another inch or two, and his mirror or bumper would have taken off [my wife’s] knee,” Holland said. “His tire literally was like so close to her that it scraped her leg and ran over her feet and both of my feet. You just can’t do that. . . . My wife has already lost one of her toenails; I’m probably going to lose a couple of mine. Her leg is kind of scraped up . . . it hurt.”

Holland took a photo of Ryan's red Ford Truck, with a Jets license plate holder and a vanity tag that says "HIT QBS."

It's entirely on brand for Ryan. Really, everything about the situation is.

Ryan faces six misdemeanors and is due in court next month. It remains to be seen whether he appears on ESPN's Sunday morning pregame show.

Then again, with the Patriots playing the Lions at 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, it's not as if anyone will be watching.

item.title: Drew Lock has another limited practice but does not have an injury designation
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Drew Lock was limited in practice Friday, his sixth consecutive practice without team drills.
item.content:encoded:
Drew Lock was limited in practice Friday, his sixth consecutive practice without team drills. Like last week, though, Lock will play through oblique and elbow injuries.

Lock does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

"He had a similar cadence and workload in terms of last week," Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Friday, via John Boyle of the team website. "It's good to have done it and gotten through the week well. I know he's confident and optimistic, so we're in good shape."

The Seahawks ruled out starter Sam Darnold (ribs/quad) for another week, but he would return after the Week 11 bye.

Offensive guard Quenton Nelson (knee), offensive tackle Charles Cross (ankle) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) also won't play.

The Seahawks are getting back outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu, receiver Rashid Shaheed and nose tackle Brandon Pili. All three were full participants Friday and do not have an injury designation.

item.title: John Harbaugh: Cam Skattebo was not supposed to push on Jameis Winston sneak
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders.
item.content:encoded:
Giants coach John Harbaugh defended running back Cam Skattebo, who stayed in his stance on a crucial Jameis Winston quarterback sneak during Thursday night's loss to the Commanders.

Harbaugh said the call was a quarterback sneak but not a tush push, and Skattebo wasn't supposed to be pushing Winston.

"We had a certain check involved in it, so he wasn’t supposed to be up there pushing. We didn't call the same [QB sneak] that we've been calling," Harbaugh said, via Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News. "What else am I supposed to say? He wasn't supposed to be up there pushing."

Why the Giants wouldn't want Skattebo to push Winston in an attempt to get the first down yardage is unclear, but the play looked strange, and it was a big one for the Giants, who had a 21-17 lead late in the fourth quarter at the time, but couldn't hold the lead after getting stuffed on that quarterback sneak and lost 24-21.

item.title: Nationwide ground stop potentially complicates NFL, college games
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Some teams could get to game locations by ground. Many would have a hard time.
item.content:encoded:
The sudden nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA will potentially impact this weekend's football games.

It's only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11. It's apparently due to a widespread outage impacting air-traffic control functions.

Visiting NFL teams typically travel to the sites of their games on Saturday; if the situation lingers, some teams may not be able to get to where they need to be. More immediately, college teams that travel on Friday have a mess.

As noted by Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area, the 49ers usually travel on Friday for games that are at least two time zones away. For Sunday's game against the Cowboys, they plan to travel on Saturday.

Some teams can get to the locations of their games by car or train. The distance from Minneapolis to Green Bay is 279 miles. For Buffalo to New Jersey (for Bills-Jets), it's also less than 300 miles.

It's roughly 290 miles fom Pittsburgh to Cincinnati, and 373 miles from L.A. to Phoenix.

For the other games (particularly Chargers-Ravens on Monday night), it's a long way to go via ground transportation.

item.title: C Hjalte Froholdt will miss his first game since joining the Cardinals
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Center Hjalte Froholdt will miss his first start since joining the Cardinals in 2023.
item.content:encoded:
Center Hjalte Froholdt will miss his first start since joining the Cardinals in 2023. Froholdt did not clear concussion protocol, ruling him out for Sunday's game against the Rams.

Froholdt had started all possible 60 games since signing as a free agent.

The Cardinals will also play without offensive lineman Jon Gaines II (ankle). That means Hayden Conner will start at center.

Defensive lineman Zach Carter, who has had three limited practices since coming off injured reserve with a knee injury, is also out.

The Cardinals list tight end Hunter Long (knee), defensive lineman Roy Lopez (toe/ankle), cornerback Max Melton (knee/hand), defensive lineman Darius Robinson (wrist), left tackle Jayden Williams (knee) and safety Dewey Wingard (groin) as questionable.

Lopez returned to practice on Friday, as did Robinson, who was a DNP on Thursday. Robinson had a wrap on his wrist.

Long would have to be activated to the 53-player roster by Saturday afternoon if he is to return this week.

item.title: Kirk Cousins will start for Vikings on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Vikings acquired the quarterback in a trade with the Raiders on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell wouldn't commit to Kirk Cousins as the team's starter earlier this week. O'Connell made it official on Friday, though, announcing Cousins will start against the Packers.

The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders at Tuesday's trade deadline, in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. He practiced with the team Thursday and Friday, but Cousins' familiarity with the offense allowed him to step right into the starting job.

Cousins was with the Vikings from 2018-23, the last two years with O'Connell. The two were also together in 2017 with Washington.

Kyler Murray started six games before he injured his hamstring. Carson Wentz started Monday night's loss to the Bills and had the worst game by a Vikings' starting quarterback since 2006.

Murray is ruled out for Sunday's game after not practicing all week.

The Vikings also ruled out linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion), tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist/chest), defensive lineman Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins (ankle) and wide receiver Jauan Jennings (calf).

Outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy (calf), wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) and safety Josh Metellus (shoulder) are questionable.

item.title: Danielle Hunter out, Will Anderson Jr. questionable for Texans-Browns
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Texans will be without at least one of their top edge rushers for Sunday's game against the Browns.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans will be without at least one of their top edge rushers for Sunday's game against the Browns.

There's a chance both will not be able to play.

Houston has listed defensive end Danielle Hunter (hamstring) as out and Will Anderson Jr. (ankle) as questionable for the contest.

Hunter and Anderson were both limited on Thursday and did not participate on Friday. That Anderson is questionable and Hunter has been ruled out suggests Hunter’s injury is more significant.

There are a few more players who have been ruled out for Houston: linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal), receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), tight end Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder).

Aside from Anderson, offensive tackle Trent Brown (illness/wrist), guard Wyatt Teller (back/illness), linebacker Jacob Hummel (groin), cornerback Jaylin Smith (hamstring), and running back David Montgomery (groin) are questionable.

Safety Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand), receiver Tank Dell (hand/shoulder), offensive tackle Blake Fisher (thumb), defensive tackle Tommy Togiai (elbow/shoulder), and running back Woody Marks (knee) are all off the injury report and are set to play.

item.title: Bills RT Spencer Brown is doubtful with ankle injury
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Bills right tackle Spencer Brown (ankle) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.
item.content:encoded:
Bills right tackle Spencer Brown (ankle) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.

Brown missed the Week 8 win over the Ravens with a back injury but returned for Monday night's win over the Vikings and played 77 of 80 snaps before his injury.

He had limited work Wednesday before sitting out Thursday and Friday. Tylan Grable will start another game if Brown can't go.

"As always, I still feel the same with a guy like Spencer, so we'll see what it looks like tomorrow. That's why we're not ruling him out," Bills coach Joe Brady said Friday, via Alec White of the team website.

Cornerback Christian Benford (wrist), defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. (shoulder), wide receiver Tyrell Shavers (knee) and defensive back Jordan Hancock (hamstring) are questionable. Shavers is in his 21-day return-to-practice window.

Left tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs) and left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) are on track to play Sunday, with full participation on Friday and no injury designation.

item.title: Kenneth Walker, Mansoor Delane are questionable for Chiefs
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Chiefs officially list running back Kenneth Walker as questionable for Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs officially list running back Kenneth Walker as questionable for Sunday.

Walker tweaked his groin sometime this week, coach Andy Reid said, and the fifth-year pro sat out Friday's practice.

"We're feeling it out just to see," Reid said, via Nate Taylor of TheAthletic.com. "We're not going to put him at risk. If he can go, he'll go. If he can't, he can't."

Walker leads the league with 109.0 rushing yards per game this season. He has 872 rushing yards with seven rushing touchdowns in eight games, and he's caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four touchdowns.

Running back Jaydn Ott is also questionable with a hamstring injury.

Rookie Emmett Johnson will start if Walker can't play.

The Chiefs also gave rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder) a questionable designation, but he had a full practice Friday. Delane was questionable to play Week 8 with the injury and was ruled out last week. He was inactive for both games.

Delane has not played since an Oct. 25 loss to the Broncos.

The Chiefs ruled out offensive lineman Jaylon Moore (ankle), defensive lineman Peter Woods (neck) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee). Norman-Lott is in his 21-day return-to-practice window.

item.title: Rams list Myles Garrett as questionable, but Sean McVay expects him to play
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Rams are listing Myles Garrett as questionable for Sunday's rematch with the Cardinals, but the club is still expecting him to play.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams are listing Myles Garrett as questionable for Sunday's rematch with the Cardinals, but the club is still expecting him to play.

Garrett will not practice on Friday, head coach Sean McVay said in his press conference, as Los Angeles is trying to keep him at his best.

"He’s feeling good," McVay said, via Gary Klein of the L.A. Times. "It's more of getting him feeling as good as possible. He’s a had a really good week, played a bunch of snaps, and expect him to be able to build on that, but we’re being smart with him."

Garrett was plenty impactful last week in his return from a knee procedure, picking up 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble.

Additionally, cornerback Trent McDuffie (back) and safety Kam Curl (toe) will be listed as questionable for the game after being limited in practice on Friday.

Guard Steve Avila (hamstring) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) have been ruled out.

item.title: Eagles will release WR Hollywood Brown, at his request
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Say goodbye to Philadelphia.
item.content:encoded:
Say goodbye to Philadelphia.

Receiver Hollywood Brown, who was available in trade but had no takers, will now be released at his request, via Tim McManus of ESPN.

Thanks to a "noninjury settlement" (which presumably includes Brown waiving his right to termination pay), Brown will be released. Because the trade deadline has passed, Brown's contract will be subject to waivers.

Brown signed a one-year deal with a $3.7 million signing bonus and a $1.3 million base salary. In addition to waiving his right to termination pay, Brown possibly agreed to return a portion of the bonus money.

A first-round pick of the Ravens in 2019, Brown appeared in only four games for the Eagles, with one start. He caught five passes for 63 yards.

Brown spent three years with the Ravens. In 2022, he was traded to the Cardinals. After two seasons in Arizona, he spent 2024 and 2025 with the Chiefs.

The minimum base salary could prompt another team to make a waivers claim — especially if that team would be willing to pay more than the prorated minimum to add him to the roster for the rest of the season.

Brown's best year came in 2021, with 91 catches for 1,008 yards and six touchdowns.

item.title: Report: Eagles to release veteran OL Fred Johnson
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Eagles are releasing veteran offensive tackle Fred Johnson, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles are releasing veteran offensive tackle Fred Johnson, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports.

The move comes shortly after veteran receiver Hollywood Brown requested his release, and the sides reached a non-injury settlement.

The Eagles have seen an overhaul of their offensive line this season.

Johnson was serving as a backup to rookie Markel Bell at right tackle since the in-season retirement of Lane Johnson. He saw action in seven games this season, playing 24 offensive snaps and 22 on special teams.

Johnson, 29, returned on a one-year contract this offseason.

He originally joined the Eagles in 2023, playing 58 games with 14 starts.

item.title: Kenneth Walker did not practice Friday with groin tightness
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: There is a potentially significant injury situation brewing with the Chiefs.
item.content:encoded:
There is a potentially significant injury situation brewing with the Chiefs.

Head coach Andy Reid told reporters in his Friday press conference that running back Kenneth Walker sat out Friday's practice after reporting tightness in his groin.

"We’ll just see how he feels through this afternoon with rehab and through tomorrow," Reid said. "Somewhere he tweaked it. So, we’ll see. ... He was tight this morning."

While Reid did not explicitly say a game status, it sounds as if Walker will be questionable.

"We’re kind of feeling it out just to see where we’re at with that thing," Reid said. "We’re not going to put him at risk or anything like that — that’s not how we roll. So, if he can go, he can go. If he can’t, he can’t."

Walker leads the league averaging 109.0 rushing yards per game. He’s tallied a total of 872 yards with seven rushing touchdowns in eight games. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four TDs.

If Walker is not able to play, rookie Emmett Johnson would be in line to start and carry the load.

“Yeah, if Emmett has to do it, then we all have [confidence],” Reid said. “He’s going to play anyway, whether Ken’s there or not there, he’s gonna play. But everybody has confidence in him, yeah.”

Johnson has 111 rushing yards on 26 carries with a touchdown and 14 receptions for 237 yards with a TD so far this year.

Kansas City’s full injury report with game statuses will be released later in the day.

item.title: Robert Saleh says he and Liam Coen are good after "misunderstanding" last year
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Titans face the Jaguars on Sunday, Robert Saleh and Liam Coen will coach against each other for the first time since their run-in last year, when they exchanged words on the field over something Saleh, then the defensive coordinator of the 49ers, said something about Coen that Coen didn't appreciate.
item.content:encoded:
When the Titans face the Jaguars on Sunday, Robert Saleh and Liam Coen will coach against each other for the first time since their run-in last year, when they exchanged words on the field over something Saleh, then the defensive coordinator of the 49ers, said something about Coen that Coen didn't appreciate.

Last year, Saleh said that Coen's team was good at stealing signals, intending it as a compliment for how good they are at recognizing what the opposing defense was doing. Coen interpreted it as an accusation of cheating and confronted Saleh on the field after the game.

Today Saleh was asked about that, and he said he and Coen have spoken and there are no hard feelings.

“Liam’s great, man," Saleh said. "We’ve had plenty of interactions. The whole thing is what it was, a little misunderstanding, poor words on my part. But they’re doing a great job. I love what they're doing offensively. They've definitely got an identity. And then [defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile] on the other side. Overall as an organization, they've done a really nice job."

Coen's confrontational approach toward Saleh after the game last year seemed like an overreaction, but no one can dispute that Coen has done a great job building the Jaguars. Saleh knows he's going up against a good coach on Sunday, and he won't provide any bulletin-board material.

item.title: John Harbaugh knew about the Jameis Winston "who let the dogs out?" cadence
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Thursday night's game between the Commanders and the Giants introduced a new wrinkle to the legend of Jameis Winston.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday night's game between the Commanders and the Giants introduced a new wrinkle to the legend of Jameis Winston.

While attempting to get the Washington defense to jump offside on a fourth-and-one play in the fourth quarter, Jameis capped his pre-snap call with, "Who let the dogs out?"

He capped it with four barks.

The move invited curiosity as to whether Jameis was simply being Jameis and seizing on the moment, or whether coach John Harbaugh knew that the homage to the Baha Men was part of the plan.

"Yeah, I knew that," Harbaugh told reporters. "That was part of the cadence, yeah. That's part of the cadence. You know, teams do jump in those situations sometimes. So that was the idea."

He's right. It seems like at least once a week a defense jumps when it knows it shouldn't. And it doesn't take much to spark the desired reaction.

Last night, it's possible that the specific cadence could have prompted one of the defenders to start laughing loud enough to tumble forward in his stance.

Regardless, it was fun. And that's when football is at its best — when it's fun.

item.title: Robert Griffin III is "expected to interview" for Baylor job
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Former Baylor quarterback Robert Griffin III is interested in coaching his former college team.
item.content:encoded:
Former Baylor quarterback Robert Griffin III is interested in coaching his former college team. And his former college team is sufficiently interested in Griffin to talk to him about it.

Via Pete Nakos of On3.com, Griffin is "expected to interview" for the vacant position.

Griffin, who won the Heisman Trophy at Baylor in 2011 before becoming the second overall pick in the 2012 NFL draft, has no coaching experience, but that hasn't been an impediment for former NFL players in recent years. Most recently, NC State hired former Wolfpack and NFL quarterback Philip Rivers, even though he has no college coaching experience. (Rivers spent the last six seasons as a high-school coach in Alabama.)

Other former players who have become college head coaches include Deion Sanders, Eddie George, and Mike Vick.

Getting an interview and getting the job are obviously two very different things. Still, Griffin has a foot in the door. Without that, it's impossible to get an invitation to the table.

item.title: Cardinals, TE Elijah Higgins agree to three-year extension
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Cardinals are investing further in the tight end position.
item.content:encoded:
The Cardinals are investing further in the tight end position.

Tight end Elijah Higgins has agreed to a three-year extension, according to a joint report from ESPN and NFL Network.

Higgins’ deal is worth up to $26.8 million and puts him under contract through 2029.

A sixth-round pick in 2023, Higgins was waived by the Dolphins at roster cuts as a rookie. But he was claimed by the Cardinals and has been with the club ever since.

Higgins has played 54 games with 23 starts, tallying 82 catches for 798 yards with four touchdowns.

Playing alongside start tight end Trey McBride, Higgins has 18 receptions for 162 yards with a touchdown in nine games so far in 2026.
